questions.question: State the rules for writing chemical symbols and give the symbols for sodium, potassium, iron, copper, silver and gold, explaining why they do not match the English names.
questions.expected_answer: A symbol has one or two letters; the first is always a capital and the second, if present, is always small (Co is cobalt, CO is carbon monoxide). Sodium Na, potassium K, iron Fe, copper Cu, silver Ag, gold Au. These come from the Latin names natrium, kalium, ferrum, cuprum, argentum and aurum, because Latin was the shared language of science when the system was created, making the symbols international.

questions.question: Define atomic number and explain why it is called an element's identity card. Name the elements with atomic numbers 1, 6, 8, 11 and 20.
questions.expected_answer: The atomic number is the number of protons in the nucleus of each atom of an element. Every atom of an element has the same number of protons and no two elements share an atomic number; changing the number of protons changes the element, so it identifies the element. 1 hydrogen (H), 6 carbon (C), 8 oxygen (O), 11 sodium (Na), 20 calcium (Ca).

questions.question: Chlorine has atomic number 17 and is in period 3, group 17. Explain what period and group mean, and describe chlorine using its position. Name the family of group 18 and give a use.
questions.expected_answer: A period is a horizontal row; a group is a vertical column, and elements in a group have similar properties. Chlorine is in the third row and the 17th column, on the right of the table, so it is a non-metal; group 17 is the halogens, reactive non-metals. Group 18 is the noble gases (helium, neon, argon), which hardly react; uses: helium in balloons, neon in lit signs, argon in light bulbs and welding.
